# Paul Irving

## Overview

- **Age:** Sixteen years old at the end of Volume 3  <sub>[v2 c1 P47](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0047), [v3 c23 P2](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0002)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v2 c1 P47](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0047)</sub>
- **Status:** Student  <sub>[v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008)</sub>
- **Origin:** United States  <sub>[v2 c1 P47](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0047)</sub>
- **Role:** Schoolboy  <sub>[v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v3 c23 P2](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0002)</sub>

## Appearance

Paul has an exceptionally delicate and refined face with big, dark blue eyes. He has chestnut curls that he wears closely cropped as he grows older. Though small for his age as a child, he grows tall and sturdy as he reaches his teens.

_Sources: [v1 c18 P35](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0035), [v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 c15 P11](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0011), [v3 c23 P2](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0002)_

## Personality

Paul is a dreamy, highly imaginative, and poetic boy who possesses an old soul. He is sensitive, gentle, and polite, with a deep capacity for affection and a serious, meditative nature. Despite his vivid imagination and quiet moments, he is manly and able to hold his own among other boys.

_Sources: [v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 c11 P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038), [v2 c15 P4](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0004), [v2 c15 P20](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0020), [v3 c28 P23](../source/v03-c28.md#nw-v03-c28-p0023)_

## Traits

- Imaginative and poetic  <sub>[v2 c11 P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038), [v2 c19 P33](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0033)</sub>
- Sensitive and delicate  <sub>[v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 c15 P1](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0001)</sub>
- Manly and athletic  <sub>[v2 c11 P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038), [v2 c23 P5](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0005)</sub>
- Polite and fair-minded  <sub>[v2 c15 P20](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0020), [v2 c19 P20](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0020)</sub>

## Abilities

- Inventing elaborate imaginative stories and imaginary friends  <sub>[v2 c11 P41](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0041), [v2 c11 P42](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0042), [v2 c19 P28](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0028)</sub>

- Playing sports like football  <sub>[v2 c11 P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038), [v2 c23 P2](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0002)</sub>

## Goals

- To reunite with his father and live together once he grows up  <sub>[v2 c15 P8](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0008)</sub>
- To grow up to be tall like his father  <sub>[v2 c15 P11](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0011), [v2 c19 P24](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0024)</sub>

## History

Paul Irving arrives in Avonlea from the United States at the age of ten to live with his grandmother, Mrs. Irving, following the death of his mother. He becomes a student at Avonlea school under Anne Shirley, with whom he instantly bonds as a kindred spirit over their shared love of imaginative concepts. He creates an intricate world of imaginary 'rock people' who live down by the shore, writing essays and stories about them. During his time in Avonlea, he also forms a close friendship with Miss Lavendar Lewis at Echo Lodge, whom he visits frequently. His father, Stephen Irving, returns to Avonlea and eventually reconciles with and marries Miss Lavendar. Following the wedding, Paul moves to Boston with his father, stepmother, and Charlotta the Fourth, though he continues to return to Avonlea and Echo Lodge for summer vacations.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P47](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0047), [v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 c5 P20](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0020), [v2 c11 P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038), [v2 c11 P41](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0041), [v2 c23 P26](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0026), [v2 c23 P30](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0030), [v2 c28 P21](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0021), [v2 c30 P10](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0010), [v2 c30 P33](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0033), [v3 c23 P1](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0001)_

## Background by volume

- Son of Stephen Irving and his deceased first wife  <sub>[v2 c1 P47](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0047), [v2 c1 P48](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0048), [v2 c15 P8](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0008)</sub>
- Raised in the United States before being sent to live with his grandmother in Avonlea at age ten  <sub>[v2 c1 P47](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0047), [v2 c11 P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038)</sub>

## Quotes

> I came back to give them to you because I thought you were the kind of lady that would like them, and because ... I like you, teacher.  <sub>[v2 c5 P20](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0020)</sub>

> You're so good at understanding, teacher. Nobody else understands so well ... not even grandma, although she's so good to me.  <sub>[v2 c15 P6](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0006)</sub>

> I think an angel walks over the world after the sun sets ... a great, tall, white angel, with silvery folded wings ... and sings the flowers and birds to sleep.  <sub>[v2 c19 P29](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0029)</sub>

> I think you would make a splendid mother. You have just the right look in your eyes ... the look my little mother always had.  <sub>[v2 c27 P20](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0020)</sub>

> It's a fine thing to have a father you can depend on, teacher.  <sub>[v2 c29 P2](../source/v02-c29.md#nw-v02-c29-p0002)</sub>
